scenario: 一个读多写少的服务把每次请求都打到数据库，热门对象反复查询，数据库 CPU 和查询延迟都在上升。
scenario_en: A read-heavy service repeatedly queries the database for hot objects, and both DB CPU and latency are rising.
q: 分布式缓存首先缓解哪条路径？
q_en: Which path does a distributed cache relieve first?
options: 把热门读请求从数据库前移到内存层
把所有写入改成跨库事务
把数据库索引全部删除
让客户端直接扫描持久化文件
options_en: Move hot reads from the database to an in-memory layer
Turn every write into a cross-database transaction
Remove all database indexes
Let clients scan persistence files directly
why: 我会先把重复热门读挡在内存缓存里，因为这样数据库只处理未命中和真实写入。但缓存不是数据源，失效和一致性要单独设计。
why_en: I would absorb repeated hot reads in memory so the database only sees misses and real writes.
whenOtherWins: 如果瓶颈来自强事务写入冲突，应该先看数据库分区、锁粒度或写入队列。
tradeoff: 读路径延迟 vs 缓存一致性成本
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C[Client] --> S[Service]
  S --> Cache[(Distributed cache)]
  Cache -- hit --> S
  Cache -- miss --> DB[(Database)]
  DB --> Cache
  S --> C

termDefinitions.meaning: DB 是持久化数据库，保存系统的权威数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A database is the durable source of truth for application data.

optionExplanations: 对，缓存的价值就是把高频重复读拦在内存这一层，别让它们每次都打到数据库。
跨库事务是保写入一致性的手段，改不了数据库被反复读中的问题。
删掉索引只会让查询更慢，缓存要挡的是读路径，不是削弱数据库能力。
让客户端绕过服务直接扫文件既不安全也不会变快，不是缓存该做的事。
optionExplanations_en: Right—caching absorbs high-frequency reads before they reach the database.
Cross-database transactions fix write consistency, not the database getting hammered by reads.
Dropping indexes only slows queries down—caching shields the read path, it doesn't gut the database.
Bypassing the service to scan files directly is unsafe and not faster—it isn't caching at all.

q: 分布式缓存通常带来哪些系统收益？
q_en: What system benefits does a distributed cache usually provide?
options: 降低热门读延迟
减少数据库读压力
天然消除所有一致性问题
可水平增加缓存节点
options_en: Lower latency for hot reads
Reduce database read pressure
Automatically remove all consistency problems
Scale out by adding cache nodes
why: 缓存的价值来自把常访问数据放近、放快、分摊到多台机器。它会引入一致性问题，不会自动消除一致性问题。
why_en: A cache helps by placing hot data closer and faster, but it adds consistency work instead of removing it.
optionExplanations: 热数据放进内存后单次读的耗时直接从磁盘/网络查询降到内存访问级别。
命中缓存的请求不用再打数据库，数据库只剩未命中和写入两类负载。
错，缓存和数据源分开存两份数据，天然会引入更新滞后，需要专门做失效和一致性设计。
键空间可以拆到更多节点，容量和吞吐能跟着加机器一起增长。
optionExplanations_en: Serving hot data from memory turns a disk/DB round trip into an in-memory lookup.
Every cache hit means one less query the database has to answer.
Wrong—cache and source hold separate copies, so staleness is introduced, not removed; it still needs invalidation design.
Splitting the keyspace across more nodes lets capacity and throughput grow as machines are added.

scenario: 缓存层的目标是毫秒级返回热门键，同时容量要覆盖工作集，成本又不能像专用硬件一样失控。
scenario_en: The cache needs millisecond-level hot-key reads, enough working-set capacity, and lower cost than specialized hardware.
q: 缓存服务器的主存储介质通常选什么？
q_en: What storage medium is usually used for cache servers?
options: 机械硬盘
RAM
离线磁带
对象存储
options_en: Hard disks
RAM
Offline tape
Object storage
why: 我会把缓存主体放在 RAM，因为随机访问延迟低，适合挡住高频读。代价是容量贵且易失，所以要靠驱逐、TTL 和必要的回源恢复。
why_en: RAM is the usual cache medium because it gives low random-access latency for hot reads.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标是低成本长期归档，而不是热读加速，对象存储或磁盘更合适。
tradeoff: 低延迟访问 vs 单位容量成本

termDefinitions.meaning: RAM 是服务器内存，访问快但断电后内容会丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Random Access Memory is fast volatile memory inside a server.

termDefinitions.meaning: TTL 是缓存条目的存活时间，到期后视为无效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time To Live is the duration after which a cache entry expires.

optionExplanations: 机械硬盘随机访问要几毫秒到十几毫秒，扛不住缓存要的毫秒内命中。
对，RAM 随机读写是微秒级，正好匹配缓存要的低延迟目标。
离线磁带要人工或机械臂上载，读取延迟是分钟到小时级，完全不是在线路径能用的。
对象存储便宜、能长期归档，但访问延迟通常是几十到上百毫秒，热读场景撑不住。
optionExplanations_en: Hard disks need single-digit to low-double-digit milliseconds per random read—too slow for cache-grade hits.
Right—RAM gives microsecond random access, matching the low-latency target a cache needs.
Offline tape needs manual or robotic mounting, so retrieval takes minutes to hours, nowhere near an online path.
Object storage is cheap for long-term archives, but tens to hundreds of milliseconds per access is too slow for hot reads.

scenario: 一个单机缓存已经装不下完整工作集，而且机器故障会让全部请求突然回源数据库。
scenario_en: A single cache node no longer fits the working set, and its failure would send all traffic back to the database.
q: 为什么要从单机缓存扩到分布式缓存？
q_en: Why move from a single cache node to a distributed cache?
options: 为了把所有数据永久持久化在缓存里
为了分摊容量和流量，并减少单点故障
为了让每个请求都绕过服务层
为了禁止应用做任何本地计算
options_en: To make the cache permanently durable
To split capacity and traffic while reducing a single point of failure
To bypass the service layer for every request
To forbid local computation in the application
why: 分布式缓存把键空间拆到多台机器，容量、吞吐和故障域都能分摊。代价是客户端路由、节点变更和一致性会更复杂。
why_en: A distributed cache splits key space and load across machines, trading simplicity for scale and fault isolation.
whenOtherWins: 如果工作集很小、故障影响可接受，单机或进程内缓存更省运维。
tradeoff: 单机简单性 vs 水平扩展与容错
optionExplanations: 缓存不是为了替代数据库做持久化，让它成为唯一权威存储反而会让丢失变成事故。
对，键空间拆到多台机器后单机故障不再拖垮整层，流量和内存压力也分开扛。
缓存扩展和服务层要不要被绕过是两回事，绕过服务会跳过鉴权和业务校验。
禁止本地计算和缓存要不要分布式没有关系，不解决容量或故障域问题。
optionExplanations_en: Making the cache the durable store isn't the goal—losing it would then mean losing real data.
Right—splitting the keyspace across nodes means one node's failure no longer takes down the whole cache.
Scaling the cache has nothing to do with skipping the service layer, which would also skip auth and validation.
Banning local computation doesn't touch capacity or fault isolation at all.

q: 缓存可以放在哪些系统层来减少重复工作？
q_en: At which layers can caching reduce repeated work?
options: Web 层：HTTP 缓存、CDN 或会话 KV
应用层：缓存计算结果或领域对象
数据库层：buffer 或查询结果缓存
日志归档层：替代所有在线读取
options_en: Web layer: HTTP cache, CDN, or session KV
Application layer: cache computed results or domain objects
Database layer: buffers or query-result cache
Archive layer: replace all online reads
why: Web、应用、数据库层都可能缓存同一条读路径上的重复工作。归档系统偏长期保存，不适合作为在线热读的主缓存层。
why_en: Caching can sit at the web, application, or database layer depending on which repeated work you want to avoid.

termDefinitions.meaning: CDN 是靠近用户的边缘缓存网络，常用于静态内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Content Delivery Network caches content near users at edge locations.

termDefinitions.meaning: KV 存储用 key 查 value，接口简单。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A key-value store retrieves a value by key.

optionExplanations: HTTP 缓存、CDN 或会话 KV 能在请求进入应用之前就把重复内容挡下来。
把计算结果或组装好的领域对象缓存住，能省掉重复的业务逻辑和聚合开销。
buffer pool 或查询结果缓存能减少同一条 SQL 反复扫盘和重新执行的成本。
错，归档层是为长期保存设计的，用它顶在线热读路径只会拖慢请求。
optionExplanations_en: HTTP caching, a CDN, or session KV catches repeat traffic before it even reaches the app.
Caching computed results or assembled domain objects skips redoing the same business logic and joins.
A buffer pool or query-result cache avoids rescanning disk and rerunning the same SQL repeatedly.
Wrong—the archive layer is built for long-term retention, not for serving online hot reads quickly.

scenario: 服务希望先查缓存，未命中才查数据库，并把结果回填缓存；缓存故障时仍可从数据库读到权威数据。
scenario_en: The service should check cache first, fall back to the database on a miss, and populate cache while keeping the DB authoritative.
q: 这条读路径最像哪种缓存模式？
q_en: Which caching pattern best matches this read path?
options: cache-aside
write-back
two-phase commit
leader election
options_en: Cache-aside
Write-back
Two-phase commit
Leader election
why: cache-aside 让应用显式处理 miss：查 DB、写缓存、返回结果。代价是应用代码要处理并发回填、TTL 和缓存失败。
why_en: Cache-aside keeps the database authoritative while the application explicitly fills cache after misses.
whenOtherWins: 如果希望缓存层自己负责回源，让业务代码只调用缓存 API，read-through 更合适。
tradeoff: 应用显式控制 vs 缓存层封装回源
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant App
  participant Cache
  participant DB
  App->>Cache: GET key
  Cache-->>App: miss
  App->>DB: read key
  DB-->>App: value
  App->>Cache: SET key ttl
  App-->>App: return value

termDefinitions.meaning: cache-aside 是应用先查缓存，miss 后查数据库并自行回填缓存的模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache-aside is a pattern where the application reads the database on a cache miss and fills the cache itself.

termDefinitions.meaning: API 是组件对外暴露的调用接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Application Programming Interface is the callable contract exposed by a component.

optionExplanations: 对，先查缓存、miss 再查数据库、然后应用自己把结果写回缓存，正是 cache-aside 的读路径。
write-back 讲的是写路径先落缓存再异步落库，不是这里描述的读优先查缓存流程。
two-phase commit 是跨系统写事务的协调协议，跟单条读请求走不走缓存没关系。
leader election 解决的是集群里谁是主节点，不涉及读请求该先查缓存还是数据库。
optionExplanations_en: Right—check cache first, fall back to the DB on a miss, then have the app fill the cache: that's cache-aside.
Write-back is about the write path landing in cache first and persisting later, not this read-first flow.
Two-phase commit coordinates a cross-system write transaction; it has nothing to do with a single read path.
Leader election decides which node is primary in a cluster—unrelated to whether a read checks cache first.

scenario: 团队想把回源逻辑封装进缓存层：业务服务只调用缓存客户端，缓存 miss 时由缓存系统加载数据库并保存结果。
scenario_en: The team wants the cache layer to own database loading on misses, while services only call the cache client.
q: 这个读策略更接近哪一种？
q_en: Which read strategy does this describe?
options: write-around
read-through
LRU
consistent hashing
options_en: Write-around
Read-through
LRU
Consistent hashing
why: read-through 把 miss 后的加载动作放进缓存层，应用拿到的是统一的 get 接口。代价是缓存层要知道数据源和加载逻辑。
why_en: Read-through hides miss loading behind the cache API, at the cost of coupling the cache to the data source.
whenOtherWins: 如果每个服务需要不同的回源、降级或序列化逻辑，cache-aside 更灵活。
tradeoff: 统一缓存接口 vs 回源逻辑耦合

termDefinitions.meaning: LRU 优先淘汰最长时间没被访问的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Least Recently Used evicts the entry that has not been accessed for the longest time.

optionExplanations: write-around 讲的是写不写缓存，不是本题在问的谁负责 miss 后加载数据。
对，让缓存层自己在 miss 时去数据库加载并保存结果，业务只调 get，这就是 read-through。
LRU 是驱逐策略，决定内存满了淘汰谁，不管 miss 时该谁去加载数据。
consistent hashing 解决的是 key 该路由到哪个节点，跟 miss 后谁负责回源无关。
optionExplanations_en: Write-around is about whether writes touch the cache, not who loads data after a read miss.
Right—when the cache itself loads from the database on a miss and the app only calls get, that's read-through.
LRU is an eviction policy deciding what to discard when memory is full, not who handles a miss.
Consistent hashing decides which node owns a key; it says nothing about who reloads on a miss.

scenario: 用户更新资料后马上刷新页面，产品要求缓存和数据库尽量同时可见，不能让用户读到旧资料。
scenario_en: After a profile update, users refresh immediately and should not read stale data from cache or database.
q: 写入策略应优先选哪一个？
q_en: Which write policy should you prefer?
options: write-back：先写缓存，稍后异步落库
write-through：同一次写入更新缓存和数据库
write-around：只写数据库，读 miss 再填缓存
random eviction：随机删缓存项
options_en: Write-back: write cache first and persist later
Write-through: update cache and database in the same write
Write-around: write DB only and fill cache on read miss
Random eviction: remove cache entries randomly
why: 我会选 write-through，因为写请求完成时缓存和数据库都已经更新。代价是写延迟更高，任一侧慢都会拖住写路径。
why_en: Write-through is the safer choice when a completed write must be visible through both cache and database.
whenOtherWins: 如果写入极多且短暂丢失可接受，write-back 可以用更低写延迟换风险。
tradeoff: 写后一致性 vs 写入延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: write-through 是写请求同时更新缓存和数据库后才返回的策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through updates both cache and database before the write is acknowledged.

optionExplanations: write-back 先认写缓存再异步落库，缓存崩溃时可能丢刚写的数据，不满足刷新就要看到新值。
对，write-through 同一次写入把缓存和数据库都更新完才返回，刷新页面能读到最新资料。
write-around 写时不进缓存，刷新页面反而会先 miss 再回源，不是最快看到新值的路径。
random eviction 是内存满了删谁的策略，跟写入要不要马上让缓存和数据库同步无关。
optionExplanations_en: Write-back acknowledges the write in cache first and persists later, risking data loss before a refresh sees it.
Right—write-through updates cache and database in the same write, so a refresh reads the new value immediately.
Write-around skips the cache on writes, so a refresh would miss first and reload—not the fastest path to freshness.
Random eviction only decides what to discard when memory is full; it doesn't touch write freshness at all.

scenario: 计数类写入非常频繁，业务能容忍短暂延迟落库，但不能让写请求被数据库延迟卡住。
scenario_en: Counter-style writes are very frequent, and the business tolerates delayed persistence but not DB latency on each write.
q: 哪种写策略最能降低写延迟？
q_en: Which write policy best reduces write latency?
options: write-through
write-around
write-back
active expiration
options_en: Write-through
Write-around
Write-back
Active expiration
why: write-back 先让缓存接住写，再异步刷到数据库，所以前台写延迟低。代价是缓存崩溃或刷盘失败时，尚未持久化的数据有丢失风险。
why_en: Write-back lowers foreground write latency by persisting to the database asynchronously.
whenOtherWins: 如果每个确认写都必须已经进数据库，write-through 更稳。
tradeoff: 低写延迟 vs 持久化风险

termDefinitions.meaning: write-back 是先写缓存并异步写数据库的策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-back writes to cache first and persists to the database later.

optionExplanations: write-through 要等缓存和数据库都写完才返回，前台写延迟反而更高，不是这里要的方向。
write-around 写时压根不进缓存，能省内存但解决不了这里最在意的写延迟问题。
对，write-back 先把写落进缓存立刻返回，数据库落盘放到后台异步做，前台写延迟最低。
active expiration 是后台清理过期条目的机制，跟这里要降低的写路径延迟没关系。
optionExplanations_en: Write-through waits for both cache and database to commit, which raises write latency, not lowers it.
Write-around skips the cache on writes, saving memory but not solving the write-latency problem here.
Right—write-back acknowledges the write in cache immediately and flushes to the database asynchronously, so foreground latency stays lowest.
Active expiration is a background cleanup mechanism for stale entries, unrelated to write-path latency.

scenario: 批量导入大量新商品，其中多数短期不会被用户读取；如果每条写都进缓存，会挤掉真正热门的数据。
scenario_en: A bulk import creates many items that are unlikely to be read soon, and caching them would evict genuinely hot data.
q: 哪种写策略能避免缓存污染？
q_en: Which write policy avoids polluting the cache?
options: write-around
read-through
write-through
LFU
options_en: Write-around
Read-through
Write-through
LFU
why: write-around 只把新值写进数据库，等真的被读到时再按 miss 回填缓存。代价是第一次读会慢一些。
why_en: Write-around keeps rarely reread writes out of cache until a real read miss happens.
whenOtherWins: 如果写后马上读是主路径，write-through 或更新后主动填缓存更合适。
tradeoff: 避免缓存污染 vs 首次读取延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: LFU 优先淘汰访问次数最少的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Least Frequently Used evicts entries with the lowest access count.

optionExplanations: 对，write-around 让批量写只落库，只有后续真被访问到才走 miss 回填，热数据不会被这批冷写挤掉。
read-through 讲的是读 miss 时谁去加载数据，不解决批量写入把缓存挤满的问题。
write-through 每次写都同时进缓存，批量导入时反而会用大量冷数据占满内存。
LFU 是淘汰访问次数最少条目的策略，跟写入该不该先进缓存是两个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Right—write-around only writes the database, so a real read miss is what fills the cache, keeping cold bulk data out.
Read-through is about who loads data on a read miss, not about writes flooding the cache.
Write-through populates the cache on every write, which is exactly what would let a bulk import evict hot data.
LFU evicts by access frequency; it doesn't decide whether writes should enter the cache at all.

scenario: 面试官让你在三个写策略里选一个，并说明一致性、延迟和缓存污染的差别。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to compare write policies by consistency, latency, and cache pollution.
q: 哪条总结最准确？
q_en: Which summary is most accurate?
options: write-through 稳但慢；write-back 快但有丢写风险；write-around 首读慢
write-through 只写缓存；write-back 只写数据库；write-around 保证强一致
write-through 不影响写延迟；write-back 不会丢数据；write-around 总能命中
write-through、write-back、write-around 都要求缓存成为唯一权威存储
options_en: Write-through is safer but slower; write-back is faster with loss risk; write-around slows first read
Write-through writes only cache; write-back writes only DB; write-around guarantees strong consistency
Write-through has no write latency cost; write-back cannot lose data; write-around always hits
Write-through, write-back, and write-around all require the cache to be the only source of truth
why: 这三个策略本质是在写延迟、一致性和缓存空间之间换。没有全局最优，必须接到业务的读写模式和可丢失风险上。
why_en: Write policies trade write latency, freshness, and cache pollution, so the right answer depends on workload.
tradeoff: 写延迟 vs 一致性 vs 缓存污染
optionExplanations: 对，这条总结把三个策略的核心取舍都点全了：write-through 稳但慢，write-back 快但可能丢写，write-around 省内存但首次读要多等一次回源。
错，说反了：write-through 缓存和数据库都写，write-back 先写缓存再异步落库，write-around 只写数据库、跳过缓存，也不保证强一致。
错，write-through 恰恰是牺牲写延迟换一致性，write-back 恰恰有丢数据窗口，write-around 也不保证总命中，这条总结把代价全说反了。
错，三种策略里数据库始终是权威存储，缓存都只是加速层，不会变成唯一权威。
optionExplanations_en: Right—this nails the tradeoffs: write-through is safe but slow, write-back is fast with loss risk, write-around costs a slower first read.

Wrong—it's backwards: write-through writes both, write-back writes cache first then persists asynchronously, and write-around writes only the database and skips the cache, without guaranteeing strong consistency.
Wrong—write-through trades latency for safety, write-back does have a loss window, and write-around doesn't guarantee hits; this flips every cost.
Wrong—in all three policies the database stays the source of truth; the cache is always just an acceleration layer.

scenario: 社交信息流里最近发布和最近查看的内容最容易再次被读，缓存内存已满。
scenario_en: In a social feed, recently posted or recently viewed items are most likely to be read again, and cache memory is full.
q: 驱逐策略优先选哪一种？
q_en: Which eviction policy should you prefer?
options: FIFO
LRU
MFU
不驱逐，等待内存无限扩容
options_en: FIFO
LRU
MFU
Never evict and wait for infinite memory
why: LRU 把最近没被碰过的数据移走，贴合“最近访问更可能再访问”的局部性。代价是如果访问模式按频率而不是最近性分布，LFU 可能更准。
why_en: LRU fits recency-heavy workloads because recently accessed items are more likely to be reused.
whenOtherWins: 如果长期高频对象比最近对象更稳定，LFU 更可能保住真正热门的数据。
tradeoff: 最近性局部性 vs 频率局部性

termDefinitions.meaning: FIFO 按进入缓存的先后顺序淘汰最早进入的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: First In, First Out evicts the entry inserted earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: MFU 优先淘汰访问次数最多的条目，适合少数特殊模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Most Frequently Used evicts entries with the highest access count.

optionExplanations: FIFO 只看进入顺序，不管这条内容是不是刚被再次访问过，贴不上这里的最近访问局部性。
对，LRU 优先淘汰最久没被碰过的条目，正好贴合最近发布或最近查看更可能再被读的模式。
MFU 反而淘汰访问最多的条目，会把这里最想留住的热门内容先删掉。
内存不可能无限扩容，不设驱逐早晚会把服务打挂，不是可行方案。
optionExplanations_en: FIFO only looks at insertion order, ignoring whether an item was just reaccessed—misses the recency pattern here.
Right—LRU evicts whatever hasn't been touched recently, matching the pattern where recent posts and views get reread.
MFU evicts the most-accessed items, which would remove exactly the hot content you want to keep.
Memory can't grow forever; refusing to evict just delays an outage instead of solving it.

q: LRU 缓存为什么常用 hash map 加双向链表？
q_en: Why does an LRU cache often combine a hash map and a doubly linked list?
text: LRU 常用 {{hash map}} 做 O(1) key 查找，用 {{双向链表}} 做 O(1) 移到头部和从尾部淘汰。
text_en: LRU often uses a {{hash map}} for O(1) key lookup and a {{doubly linked list}} for O(1) move-to-front and tail eviction.
why: hash map 负责快查，链表负责维护访问顺序。双向链表删除中间节点不需要从头扫描。
why_en: The hash map finds entries quickly, while the doubly linked list updates recency order in constant time.

termDefinitions.meaning: hash map 是按 key 快速定位 value 或节点指针的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash map is a data structure that locates a value or node pointer by key.

scenario: 缓存条目都有 TTL。团队在比较后台定期清理过期 key，还是等请求命中 key 时再检查过期。
scenario_en: Cache entries have TTLs, and the team is comparing background expiry scans with checking expiry only when a key is requested.
q: active 与 passive expiration 的区别是什么？
q_en: How do active and passive expiration differ?
options: active 后台扫过期项，passive 在访问时检查并删除
active 只用于数据库，passive 只用于 CDN
active 永不删除数据，passive 立即删除所有数据
active 是写策略，passive 是分片策略
options_en: Active scans expired entries in the background; passive checks and removes on access
Active is only for databases, while passive is only for CDNs
Active never deletes data, while passive deletes all data immediately
Active is a write policy, while passive is a sharding policy
why: active expiration 用后台工作提前清理，减少过期数据占内存；passive expiration 把检查推迟到访问时，后台成本更低但过期项可能多留一阵。
why_en: Active expiration spends background work to clean earlier, while passive expiration delays cleanup until access.
tradeoff: 后台清理成本 vs 过期项滞留
optionExplanations: 对，active 靠后台任务定期扫清过期 key，passive 把检查推迟到有请求访问时才做，这是两者的分工。
错，active 和 passive 是通用的过期回收方式，不是按存储类型强绑定数据库或 CDN。
错，两者都会删过期数据，区别只在何时删，不是一个永不删一个删光所有数据。
错，active/passive 描述的是过期回收的触发方式，跟写入策略或分片策略是两个维度。
optionExplanations_en: Right—active means a background job periodically sweeps expired keys, while passive checks and evicts only when a key is accessed.
Wrong—active and passive are general expiry mechanisms, not tied specifically to databases versus CDNs.
Wrong—both eventually remove expired entries; the difference is timing, not one never removing and one removing everything.
Wrong—active/passive describe when expiry is triggered, a different axis from write policy or sharding.

scenario: 缓存集群经常扩缩容。用 hash(key) % N 时，N 一变，大多数 key 都会换节点，导致大量缓存失效。
scenario_en: The cache cluster scales often; with hash(key) % N, changing N remaps most keys and causes massive cache invalidation.
q: 路由 key 到节点应优先用什么？
q_en: What should route keys to nodes?
options: 随机选节点
consistent hashing
每个客户端维护不同节点列表
把所有 key 固定放第一台机器
options_en: Pick a random node
Consistent hashing
Let each client keep a different server list
Put every key on the first machine
why: consistent hashing 让节点变化时只迁移环上相邻的一小段 key，避免扩容变成全量冷启动。代价是实现和负载均衡比简单取模更复杂。
why_en: Consistent hashing limits remapping when nodes change, avoiding a broad cache cold start.
whenOtherWins: 如果节点数固定且系统很小，简单取模更容易实现。
tradeoff: 节点变更稳定性 vs 路由复杂度
diagram:
flowchart LR
  K[key] --> H[hash]
  H --> Ring[hash ring]
  Ring --> N1[Node A]
  Ring --> N2[Node B]
  Ring --> N3[Node C]
  N2 -.add/remove moves nearby keys.-> Ring

termDefinitions.meaning: consistent hashing 用 hash 环分配 key，节点变化时尽量少迁移 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps keys on a hash ring so node changes move only a limited key range.

optionExplanations: 随机选节点会让同一个 key 的 PUT 和后续 GET 落到不同机器，读根本找不到刚写的值。
对，它只让新增或移除节点附近那一小圈 key 换地方，其余映射保持不动，不用像取模那样全量重排。
每个客户端各看各的节点列表会让同一个 key 在不同客户端眼里路由到不同机器，直接破坏一致性。
把所有 key 都塞进第一台机器，容量和热点全压在单点，扩容和多节点变得毫无意义。
optionExplanations_en: Random node selection means a PUT and a later GET for the same key can land on different machines and miss.
Right—consistent hashing limits remapping to a small ring segment when nodes change, avoiding a full cache reset.
If each client sees a different node list, the same key routes to different machines depending on who's asking.
Pinning every key to one machine concentrates capacity and hot traffic on a single node, defeating the point of adding nodes.

q: 为什么所有缓存客户端必须共享同一份节点视图？
q_en: Why must all cache clients share the same cluster view?
text: 如果客户端的 {{hashing algorithm}} 或 {{server list}} 不一致，同一个 key 的 PUT 和 GET 可能落到不同缓存节点。
text_en: If clients disagree on the {{hashing algorithm}} or {{server list}}, a PUT and later GET for the same key may hit different cache nodes.
why: 缓存客户端是路由入口，路由不一致会表现成随机 miss 或旧值。配置服务的核心价值就是让客户端看到同一套集群状态。
why_en: Cache clients must agree on routing, otherwise the same key may be written to one node and read from another.

termDefinitions.meaning: PUT 在这里表示把某个 key-value 写入缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PUT means writing a key-value entry into the cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: GET 在这里表示按 key 从缓存读取 value。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GET means reading a value from the cache by key.

scenario: 公司有多个服务要共享缓存，并希望缓存机器按内存优化、应用机器按 CPU 优化，两层能独立扩容。
scenario_en: Several services share the cache, and the company wants memory-optimized cache nodes and CPU-optimized app nodes to scale independently.
q: 缓存部署方式更适合哪一种？
q_en: Which cache deployment model fits better?
options: 专用缓存服务器
只在每个应用进程内放本地缓存
把缓存和数据库合并成同一进程
每次请求都新建一个缓存节点
options_en: Dedicated cache servers
Only local in-process cache inside each app
Merge cache and database into one process
Create a new cache node per request
why: 专用缓存服务器让应用层和缓存层按不同资源画像扩容，也更适合做共享的 Cache as a Service。代价是多一次网络跳转和独立运维成本。
why_en: Dedicated cache servers let app and cache tiers scale by different resource needs.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统很小、成本极敏感，且缓存只服务本机应用，co-located cache 更便宜。
tradeoff: 独立扩容与共享服务 vs 网络跳转与运维成本

termDefinitions.meaning: Cache as a Service 是多个应用共享的一套缓存集群，通常要做 key 命名隔离。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache as a Service is a shared cache cluster used by multiple applications, usually with key namespacing.

optionExplanations: 对，专用缓存服务器能单独按内存画像扩容，和按 CPU 画像扩容的应用层解耦。
本地进程内缓存不能跨服务共享，也没法按内存单独扩容，撑不住多服务共享的目标。
把缓存和数据库塞进一个进程，两层就没法各自按不同资源画像独立扩容了。
每个请求都新建节点会让节点数量随流量暴涨，根本不是可维护的部署方式。
optionExplanations_en: Right—dedicated cache servers can scale by memory profile independently of the CPU-profiled app tier.
In-process local caches can't be shared across services or scaled by memory alone, missing the shared-cache goal.
Merging cache and database into one process removes the ability to scale each tier by its own resource profile.
Spinning up a new node per request would make node count explode with traffic—not a workable deployment.

scenario: 同一套共享缓存集群服务支付、推荐和用户资料三个团队，大家都可能使用 user:123 这种 key。
scenario_en: A shared cache cluster serves payments, recommendations, and profiles, and several teams may use keys like user:123.
q: 共享缓存最需要哪种隔离手段？
q_en: What isolation mechanism is most needed in a shared cache?
options: key namespacing
禁用所有 TTL
把所有 key 改成随机数且不记录映射
让每个团队修改缓存服务器源码
options_en: Key namespacing
Disable every TTL
Use random keys without storing mappings
Let each team modify the cache server source code
why: 命名空间把 key 前缀按服务或租户隔开，避免不同团队覆盖彼此的缓存项。它不解决容量争抢，所以还要配额和监控。
why_en: Key namespacing prevents teams from accidentally overwriting each other's entries in a shared cache.
tradeoff: 共享缓存效率 vs 租户隔离

termDefinitions.meaning: key namespacing 是给 key 加服务或租户前缀来避免命名冲突。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key namespacing prefixes keys by service or tenant to avoid collisions.

optionExplanations: 对，给 key 加服务或租户前缀，通用命名像 user:123 就不会被别的团队意外覆盖。
禁用 TTL 只影响过期回收，跟不同团队的 key 会不会互相冲突覆盖没关系。
key 改成随机数又不记录映射，等于自己都找不回自己写的数据，比冲突还糟。
让每个团队各自改缓存服务器源码，既解决不了命名冲突，还会让集群难以统一维护。
optionExplanations_en: Right—prefixing keys by service or tenant means a generic key like user:123 won't get overwritten by another team.
Disabling every TTL only affects expiry cleanup, not whether different teams' keys collide.
Randomizing keys without storing the mapping means you can't find your own data again—worse than a collision.
Letting every team patch the cache server source code doesn't fix naming collisions and makes the cluster unmaintainable.

scenario: 候选人把缓存和通用 key-value 数据库混为一谈，面试官追问两者边界。
scenario_en: A candidate treats a cache and a general key-value database as the same thing, and the interviewer asks for the boundary.
q: 缓存和持久 KV 存储的关键区别是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between a cache and a durable key-value store?
options: 缓存通常是临时内存副本，KV 数据库负责持久化
缓存只能存图片，KV 只能存 SQL 表
缓存一定比 KV 更强一致
KV 必须没有 key
options_en: A cache is usually a temporary in-memory copy; a KV database is the durable one
A cache can only store images, while a KV store can only store SQL tables
A cache is always more strongly consistent than a KV store
A KV store must not have keys
why: 两者接口都可能是 get/put，但缓存可以被驱逐、过期或重建。持久 KV 存储通常要保证数据长期存在。
why_en: The API can look similar, but a cache is disposable while a durable KV store is a source of stored state.
tradeoff: 临时加速层 vs 持久状态层

termDefinitions.meaning: KV 是用 key 直接读取 value 的存储接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key-value storage retrieves values directly by key.

optionExplanations: 对，缓存通常可被驱逐或重建，持久 KV 存储要保证数据长期存在，这是两者的关键分界。
错，接口都可能是 get/put，能存的内容类型不是按图片还是表结构划分的。
错，缓存恰恰更容易旧值和驱逐，一致性通常比专门设计的持久存储更弱，不是更强。
错，key-value 存储的定义就是靠 key 取 value，没有 key 这个说法本身就自相矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: Right—a cache can be evicted or rebuilt, while a durable KV store must keep data around long-term; that's the real boundary.
Wrong—both expose get/put style APIs, and content type isn't split along images versus SQL tables.
Wrong—a cache is more prone to staleness and eviction, so it's usually weaker on consistency, not stronger.
Wrong—a key-value store is defined by looking up values by key; 'no keys' contradicts the whole concept.

scenario: 缓存节点会自动扩缩容和故障替换。你不希望每次节点变化都靠人工改配置并重启所有服务。
scenario_en: Cache nodes are added, removed, and replaced automatically; you do not want manual config edits and service restarts for every change.
q: 客户端维护缓存节点列表应选什么方案？
q_en: How should clients maintain the cache server list?
options: 每台机器一个手写本地配置文件
集中配置文件但仍靠人工更新健康状态
配置服务监控节点并通知客户端
让客户端永远假设只有一台缓存机
options_en: A handwritten local config file on each host
A centralized config file with manually updated health
A configuration service that monitors nodes and notifies clients
Have clients forever assume there is one cache server
why: 配置服务能把节点增删和健康变化及时推给客户端，避免路由长期停留在坏节点上。代价是多一个高可用组件要设计和运维。
why_en: A configuration service keeps client routing current as cache nodes join, leave, or fail.
whenOtherWins: 如果集群很小且节点几乎不变，本地或集中配置文件可以先撑住。
tradeoff: 自动发现与健康传播 vs 配置服务复杂度
optionExplanations: 每台机器各写一份配置，节点一变就要逐台手动改，跟不上自动扩缩容的速度。
集中文件省了分发麻烦，但健康状态还是靠人工更新，节点故障后仍要等人发现。
对，配置服务持续探活并主动推送节点变化，客户端能及时避开坏节点或用上新节点。
让客户端永远只认一台缓存机，节点一多或一换就直接找不到数据了。
optionExplanations_en: A hand-edited file per machine needs manual updates on every node change—too slow for auto-scaling.
A centralized file avoids redistributing config, but health still needs a human to update it after a failure.
Right—a configuration service actively probes health and pushes membership changes, so clients avoid bad nodes quickly.
Assuming there's forever only one cache server breaks the moment nodes are added, removed, or replaced.

q: 缓存节点故障时，配置服务到客户端的正确状态链是什么？
q_en: What is the correct state chain when a cache node fails?
steps: 客户端按旧列表继续把部分 key 路由到这台坏节点。
配置服务或监控探测到节点不可用。
客户端收到新列表后重算路由；受影响 key 可能 miss 并回源。
缓存节点宕机或网络隔离。
配置服务发布新的可用节点列表。
why: 这条链要讲清楚中间的不一致窗口：故障先发生，客户端视图随后才收敛。代价是窗口内会有 miss、超时或回源压力。
why_en: Membership changes are not instant, so clients may route to a failed node until the configuration view converges.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  F[Node fails] --> Old[Clients use old list]
  Old --> Detect[Config service detects]
  Detect --> Push[Publish new list]
  Push --> Rehash[Clients rehash]
  Rehash --> Miss[Misses refill from DB]

scenario: 一个缓存分片的主节点宕机时，团队希望还能读到该分片的大部分热门数据，并把热分片读流量分散出去。
scenario_en: When a cache shard's primary fails, the team wants most hot data still readable and hot-shard reads spread out.
q: 分片内部应加入什么结构？
q_en: What structure should each shard add?
options: 一个 primary 加多个 replica
只保留一个节点、完全不设置备份
每次读都要全量扫描所有分片数据
把所有缓存分片直接合并进数据库进程
options_en: One primary with multiple replicas
Keep just one node with absolutely no backup
Scan every shard in full on every single read
Merge every cache shard directly into the database process
why: primary-replica 能在主节点故障时保留副本，也能让读流量分摊到多个节点。代价是复制延迟和副本一致性要处理。
why_en: Primary-replica shards improve availability and read scaling, but introduce replication lag and consistency work.
whenOtherWins: 如果缓存完全可丢且回源数据库很轻，单副本缓存能省成本。
tradeoff: 可用性与读扩展 vs 复制成本与一致性
diagram:
flowchart TB
  Client --> P[(Primary)]
  P --> R1[(Replica A)]
  P --> R2[(Replica B)]
  Client -.read.-> R1
  Client -.read.-> R2

termDefinitions.meaning: replica 是主数据的副本节点，用来承担读或故障接管。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica is a copy of primary data used for reads or failover.

optionExplanations: 对，一个 primary 配多个 replica，主节点故障时副本还能顶上，读流量也能分摊到多台。
只保留一个节点、完全不设置备份，主节点一宕机这个分片的数据就直接不可读了。
每次读都要全量扫描所有分片数据，等于放弃了分片和索引带来的加速，延迟会暴涨。
把所有缓存分片直接合并进数据库进程，缓存独立扩容和低延迟内存访问的优势也就没了。
optionExplanations_en: Right—one primary with multiple replicas keeps data readable if the primary fails and spreads read load across nodes.
Keeping just one node with absolutely no backup means the shard's data becomes unreadable the moment that node fails.
Scanning every shard in full on every single read throws away the whole point of sharding and indexing—latency would spike.
Merging every cache shard directly into the database process gives up the cache's independent scaling and low-latency access.

scenario: 同一数据中心内 primary 和 replica 网络距离很近，系统希望写返回后副本也尽量已经有新值。
scenario_en: Within one data center, primary and replicas are close, and the system wants replicas updated before a write returns.
q: 同城缓存副本写入可考虑哪种复制？
q_en: Which replication style can be considered within one data center?
options: 同步复制到近距离副本
跨洲同步复制每个缓存写
完全不复制
只在客户端浏览器复制
options_en: Synchronous replication to nearby replicas
Synchronous replication across continents for every cache write
No replication at all
Replicate only in the user's browser
why: 同 DC 内 RTT 小，同步复制的延迟成本可能可接受，能换来更强的副本新鲜度。距离变远后，同步写会把网络往返直接加到写延迟上。
why_en: Synchronous replication can work inside one data center because the network round trip is small enough.
whenOtherWins: 如果副本跨地域，通常改用异步复制并接受短暂旧值。
tradeoff: 副本新鲜度 vs 写入尾延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: DC 是同一机房或同一区域的数据中心。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data center is a facility or region hosting servers and networking.

termDefinitions.meaning: RTT 是一次网络请求往返所需时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Round-Trip Time is the time for a network request to go out and return.

optionExplanations: 对，同一数据中心内 RTT 很小，同步等副本写完再返回是可接受的延迟成本，能换到更强新鲜度。
跨洲同步复制会把几十上百毫秒的远距离往返直接加进每次写的响应时间，写延迟会失控。
完全不复制在这里连最基本的主节点故障保护都没有，谈不上新鲜度。
只在用户浏览器里复制解决不了服务器端多副本要不要同步一致的问题，范围完全不对。
optionExplanations_en: Right—inside one data center the round trip is small, so waiting for the replica before returning is an acceptable cost for freshness.
Synchronous replication across continents adds tens to hundreds of milliseconds of wide-area RTT to every single write.
No replication at all leaves you without even basic primary-failure protection, let alone freshness.
Replicating only inside the user's browser doesn't address server-side replica consistency at all—wrong layer entirely.

scenario: 缓存要跨两个数据中心容灾。业务要求读延迟低，能接受跨地域副本短暂落后。
scenario_en: The cache must survive two data centers; reads should stay low-latency, and cross-region replicas may lag briefly.
q: 跨数据中心复制通常怎么选？
q_en: How is cross-data-center cache replication usually chosen?
options: 每次写都跨 DC 同步提交
跨 DC 异步复制，并监控复制延迟
不设副本，只靠用户重试
让数据库删除所有源数据
options_en: Synchronously commit every write across data centers
Replicate asynchronously across data centers and monitor lag
Use no replicas and rely only on user retries
Delete all source data from the database
why: 跨 DC 同步写会把远距离 RTT 放进写路径，缓存通常不值得为它牺牲低延迟。异步复制保住可用性和速度，但要接受 eventual consistency。
why_en: Cross-DC cache replication is usually asynchronous because synchronous writes add high wide-area latency.
whenOtherWins: 如果是金融账本这类不能读旧值的权威数据，应该在数据库层设计强一致，而不是靠缓存跨 DC 同步。
tradeoff: 跨地域低延迟与可用性 vs 强一致

termDefinitions.meaning: eventual consistency 表示副本可能短暂不同，但在没有新写入后会逐步收敛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means replicas may temporarily differ but converge if no new writes occur.

optionExplanations: 跨 DC 每次写都同步提交，会把跨地域 RTT 直接加进写路径，跟这里要的低延迟读矛盾。
对，跨 DC 异步复制既保住本地低延迟读，又能靠监控复制延迟把可接受的滞后窗口量化。
不设副本靠用户自己重试，一旦一个 DC 挂了数据就直接读不到，不是容灾方案。
让数据库删掉所有源数据完全是反向操作，不解决容灾复制，反而制造数据丢失。
optionExplanations_en: Committing every write synchronously across data centers pushes wide-area RTT into the write path, fighting the low-latency goal.
Right—asynchronous cross-DC replication keeps local reads fast while lag monitoring bounds how stale replicas can get.
No replicas and relying on user retries means data is simply gone if one data center fails—that's not disaster recovery.
Deleting all source data from the database is the opposite of replication and just causes data loss.

scenario: 一个 replica 在写入期间离线，几分钟后恢复。它本地缓存里仍有旧值，但还没追上 primary 的最新状态。
scenario_en: A replica was offline during writes and comes back with stale local entries before catching up to the primary.
q: 恢复中的副本应该怎样处理请求？
q_en: How should a recovering replica handle requests?
options: 立刻服务所有读请求
在同步完成前不对外服务或只服务安全范围
删除 primary 上的新值来匹配旧副本
把旧值广播给所有客户端作为最新值
options_en: Serve all reads immediately
Stay out of service, or serve only safe ranges, until it is synchronized
Delete new values on the primary to match the old replica
Broadcast stale values to all clients as current
why: 恢复节点的危险不是宕机，而是带着旧数据重新加入读池。先同步再服务，可以避免把已更新的 key 又读回旧版本。
why_en: A recovering replica should not serve stale data before it has caught up with the primary.
tradeoff: 快速恢复容量 vs 避免旧值读出
optionExplanations: 刚恢复就立刻接读请求，会把还没追上的旧值当成最新值返回给用户。
对，先把自己排除在读池外或只服务确定安全的范围，等追上 primary 再全量服务，能避免读到旧版本。
删掉 primary 上已经生效的新值去迁就落后的副本，等于主动制造数据倒退。
把旧值当最新值广播给所有客户端，会让整个系统集体读到过期数据，比单副本旧值更糟。
optionExplanations_en: Serving all reads the instant it's back means users get stale values that haven't caught up yet as if they were current.
Right—staying out of the read pool (or serving only a known-safe range) until it's caught up avoids returning old versions.
Deleting already-committed new values on the primary to match a lagging replica is deliberately rolling data backward.
Broadcasting stale values to every client as current would spread staleness system-wide, worse than one lagging replica.

scenario: 一个明星事件让 key=taylor:latest 的读流量暴涨。consistent hashing 把这个 key 固定路由到同一个分片，单节点 CPU 和网卡被打满。
scenario_en: A celebrity event makes key=taylor:latest extremely hot; consistent hashing routes it to one shard, saturating one node's CPU and network.
q: 热 key 最直接的缓解是什么？
q_en: What is the most direct mitigation for a hot key?
options: 给热 key 做动态复制或拆成多个读副本
把所有其他 key 删除
关闭所有缓存，让数据库扛流量
让客户端随机写不同值
options_en: Dynamically replicate the hot key or split it across read replicas
Delete every other key
Disable all caches and let the database absorb traffic
Have clients randomly write different values
why: 热 key 的问题是单个 key 的读无法靠普通分片继续分摊。复制热 key 让多台机器共同承担读，但要处理更新传播和短暂旧值。
why_en: A hot key needs extra read copies because normal sharding cannot split one key across nodes.
whenOtherWins: 如果热点来自一个 key 范围而不是单 key，增加虚拟节点或重新分片更合适。
tradeoff: 热点读扩散 vs 更新一致性
optionExplanations: 对，给这个热 key 单独加读副本，读压力能从一台机器摊到多台，普通分片解决不了单 key 的问题。
删掉其他无关 key 腾不出这台机器的 CPU 和网卡带宽，热 key 本身的压力还在同一节点上。
关掉所有缓存会让这波热流量直接砸向数据库，等于把局部问题扩大成全局故障。
让客户端各自写不同值，会让同一个 key 在不同副本上出现互相矛盾的内容。
optionExplanations_en: Right—giving the hot key extra read replicas spreads the load across machines, since normal sharding can't split one key.
Deleting unrelated keys frees no CPU or network bandwidth on the node still absorbing the hot key's traffic.
Disabling every cache sends this spike straight at the database, turning a local hotspot into a system-wide outage.
Having clients write different values independently would leave replicas holding conflicting content for the same key.

scenario: consistent hashing 后，某些物理节点因为环上区间太大而承担更多 key，负载分布明显不均。
scenario_en: After consistent hashing, some physical nodes own larger ring ranges and carry noticeably more keys.
q: 如何让分片负载更均匀？
q_en: How can shard load be made more even?
options: 给每台物理机放多个 virtual node
把 hash 函数改成恒定返回 0
让所有客户端使用不同 hash 函数
只保留负载最高的节点
options_en: Place multiple virtual nodes per physical machine
Make the hash function always return zero
Let every client use a different hash function
Keep only the highest-load node
why: virtual node 让一台物理机在 hash 环上占多个小位置，区间更碎，统计上更容易均匀。代价是路由表和迁移管理更复杂。
why_en: Virtual nodes spread each physical server across the hash ring, smoothing uneven key ranges.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有两三台机器且负载很小，先用简单 consistent hashing 也可以。
tradeoff: 负载均衡平滑度 vs 路由元数据复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: virtual node 是物理缓存节点在 hash 环上的多个逻辑位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A virtual node is a logical position representing a physical server on a hash ring.

optionExplanations: 对，每台物理机在环上占多个小区间后，统计上大区间的偏差会被摊平，负载更均匀。
hash 函数恒定返回同一个值，所有 key 会挤到环上同一点，负载反而变成极端不均。
客户端各用不同 hash 函数会让同一个 key 在不同客户端眼里路由到不同节点，直接破坏路由一致性。
只留负载最高的节点，等于把所有流量都塞给最忙的那台，问题只会更严重。
optionExplanations_en: Right—giving each physical machine several ring positions statistically smooths out uneven ranges into more even load.
A hash function that always returns the same value piles every key onto one ring point—the opposite of even load.
If every client uses a different hash function, the same key routes to different nodes depending on who's asking.
Keeping only the highest-load node just dumps all traffic onto the already-busiest machine—that makes it worse.

q: 数据库删除一行时，缓存显式 delete 的正确闭环是什么？
q_en: What is the correct cache-invalidation chain when a database row is deleted?
steps: 后续读请求 miss，再从数据库确认不存在或加载新状态。
缓存节点删除对应 key，或让该 key 失效。
服务收到删除业务请求并先更新权威数据库。
如果缓存 delete 失败，系统记录重试或用短 TTL 限制旧值窗口。
服务向缓存发送显式 delete/invalidate。
why: 删除不同于普通驱逐：源数据已经不存在，旧缓存继续命中会把已删除对象读回来。失败时要有重试或短 TTL 收口旧值窗口。
why_en: Deletes need explicit invalidation because a stale cache hit can resurrect data that no longer exists in the database.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant S as Service
  participant DB
  participant C as Cache
  S->>DB: delete row
  DB-->>S: committed
  S->>C: delete key
  C-->>S: ack or retry needed
  S-->>S: future read misses

termDefinitions.meaning: invalidate 是让缓存项失效，使后续读取不能直接使用旧值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Invalidate means marking a cache entry unusable so future reads cannot use the old value.

q: 单台缓存服务器内部的典型数据结构组合是什么？
q_en: What is the typical internal data-structure combination inside one cache server?
options: hash table 快查，双向链表维护 LRU
排序文本文件服务读，再用脚本定期重排
每次请求遍历全部 value，并按时间过滤
只用消息队列保存当前缓存和驱逐顺序
options_en: A hash table looks up keys, and a linked list tracks LRU
A sorted text file serves reads, with scripts periodically reordering it
Every request scans all values and filters by time
A message queue alone stores current cache state and eviction order
why: hash table 给平均 O(1) 查找，链表让 LRU 这类策略在访问和淘汰时 O(1) 更新。全量扫描会把缓存的低延迟目标打掉。
why_en: A hash table plus a doubly linked list supports fast lookup and constant-time recency updates.

termDefinitions.meaning: O(1) 表示操作耗时不随缓存项数量线性增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(1) means the operation time does not grow linearly with the number of entries.

optionExplanations: 对，用 hash table 定位 key 平均只要常数时间，再用双向链表把最近使用顺序的增删也压到常数时间，两者一起才够快。
排序文本文件加脚本重排属于批处理思路，单次读写延迟是毫秒到秒级，跟缓存要的响应速度不在一个量级。
每次请求都遍历全部 value 再过滤，查找退化成 O(n)，请求量一大延迟就线性劣化。
消息队列擅长顺序传递消息，不是为按 key 随机查找设计的结构，不适合当主存储索引。
optionExplanations_en: Right—a hash table gives average O(1) lookup and a doubly linked list keeps LRU bookkeeping O(1); together they support low latency.
A sorted text file with periodic script reordering is a batch-processing idea, with millisecond-to-second latency, not cache-grade.
Scanning every value on every request degrades lookup to O(n), so latency grows linearly with request volume.
A message queue is built for ordered delivery, not random key lookup—wrong structure for the primary index.

q: EAT 如何把命中率转成平均访问延迟？
q_en: How does EAT turn hit rate into average access latency?
text: EAT = {{hit ratio × hit time + miss ratio × miss time}}；如果 hit=5ms、miss=30ms，miss 从 10% 降到 5% 会把平均延迟从 7.5ms 降到 6.25ms。
text_en: EAT = {{hit ratio × hit time + miss ratio × miss time}}; with hit=5ms and miss=30ms, reducing misses from 10% to 5% lowers average latency from 7.5ms to 6.25ms.
why: EAT = Effective Access Time，用命中和未命中的加权平均估算读延迟。这个数用于比较驱逐策略是否真的降低用户读延迟，而不是只看算法名字。
why_en: Effective Access Time is the weighted average latency of hits and misses, so hit-rate gains translate directly into user-visible latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: EAT 是命中和未命中路径按比例加权后的平均访问时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Effective Access Time is the weighted average access latency across hits and misses.

scenario: 压测里 hit=5ms、miss=30ms。策略 A 的 miss ratio 是 10%，策略 B 是 5%，其他开销接近。
scenario_en: In a benchmark, hits take 5 ms and misses take 30 ms; policy A has 10% misses and policy B has 5%, with similar overhead.
q: 应该优先采用哪种策略？
q_en: Which policy should you prefer?
options: 策略 A，因为 miss 更多说明更公平
策略 B，因为 EAT 更低
两者完全一样，因为 hit time 相同
删除缓存，因为 miss time 比 hit time 大
options_en: Policy A because more misses are fairer
Policy B because its EAT is lower
They are identical because hit time is the same
Remove the cache because misses are slower than hits
why: 策略 A 的 EAT 是 0.9×5+0.1×30=7.5ms，策略 B 是 0.95×5+0.05×30=6.25ms。这个差距会直接进入平均读延迟。
why_en: Policy B wins because its lower miss ratio reduces the weighted average access time.
whenOtherWins: 如果策略 B 的维护 CPU 或锁竞争远高于 A，就要把算法开销也放进压测。
tradeoff: 命中率收益 vs 驱逐维护成本

termDefinitions.meaning: miss ratio 是缓存未命中的请求比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Miss ratio is the fraction of requests not served from cache.

optionExplanations: miss 更多不是公平不公平的问题，它直接意味着更多请求要走慢速的 30ms 路径。
对，B 的 miss 只占 5%，比 A 的 10% 更少扛慢速的 30ms 路径，摊出来的平均延迟更低。
hit time 一样不代表整体延迟一样，miss ratio 不同会让加权平均结果完全不同。
miss 比 hit 慢不是删缓存的理由，删了之后所有请求都变成 30ms 级的慢路径。
optionExplanations_en: More misses isn't about fairness—it directly means more requests take the slow 30ms path.
Right—B only sends 5% of requests down the slow 30ms path versus A's 10%, so its blended average latency is lower.
Equal hit time doesn't mean equal overall latency—different miss ratios change the weighted average completely.
Misses being slower than hits isn't a reason to remove the cache—every request would then take the slow 30ms path.

q: 哪些机制共同支撑分布式缓存的高性能？
q_en: Which mechanisms together support high performance in a distributed cache?
options: 内存服务热门读
hash table 做本机 O(1) 查找
LRU 更新用双向链表保持 O(1)
每次读都同步写入跨洲副本
options_en: Serve hot reads from memory
Use hash tables for average O(1) local lookup
Use a doubly linked list for O(1) LRU updates
Synchronously write cross-continent replicas on every read
why: 高性能来自命中路径短、本机查找快、驱逐维护轻。跨洲同步会把远距离网络延迟塞进热路径。
why_en: The fast path stays fast when reads hit memory and local bookkeeping is constant time.
optionExplanations: 热数据留在内存里，读路径就不用再等一次磁盘或数据库查询。
hash table 让本机查找不用线性扫描，平均一次查找就能定位到目标 key。
双向链表让每次访问后调整最近使用顺序也是常数时间，不会随缓存项变多而变慢。
错，每次读都同步写跨洲副本，会把跨地域网络延迟直接加进本该很快的读路径。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping hot data in memory means the read path skips a disk or database round trip entirely.
A hash table means local lookups don't need a linear scan—one lookup finds the target key on average.
A doubly linked list keeps recency updates constant-time too, so it doesn't slow down as entries grow.
Wrong—synchronously replicating across continents on every read injects wide-area latency into what should be a fast path.

scenario: 缓存分片都有 primary 和两个 replica，但三者都部署在同一个数据中心。
scenario_en: Each cache shard has a primary and two replicas, but all three are deployed in the same data center.
q: 这套副本方案还缺什么容灾能力？
q_en: What disaster-recovery ability is still missing?
options: 单节点故障容忍
整个数据中心故障容忍
读流量分摊
缓存项驱逐
options_en: Single-node failure tolerance
Whole-data-center failure tolerance
Read traffic spreading
Cache entry eviction
why: 同 DC 多副本能抗机器故障，但抗不了机房断电、网络隔离或区域级事故。跨 DC 副本能提高可用性，但通常要接受异步复制和旧值窗口。
why_en: Replicas in one data center handle node failures, not a full data-center outage.
tradeoff: 单 DC 低延迟 vs 跨 DC 容灾
optionExplanations: 单节点故障容忍已经有了，primary 加两个 replica 本来就能扛住机器级故障。
对，三个副本全在同一个 DC，机房断电或网络隔离会让整个分片一起不可用，这是还缺的能力。
读流量分摊也已经具备，多个副本本身就能分担读请求。
缓存项驱逐是内存满了淘汰谁的问题，跟副本部署在几个数据中心完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Single-node failure tolerance is already covered—a primary plus two replicas handles machine-level failures.
Right—since all three copies sit in one data center, a power or network outage there takes the whole shard down; that's the missing piece.
Read traffic spreading is already handled too, since multiple replicas can share read load.
Cache eviction is about what to discard when memory fills up—unrelated to how many data centers replicas span.

scenario: 跨数据中心缓存复制遇到网络分区。业务宁愿短暂读旧值，也要保持本地读取低延迟和服务可用。
scenario_en: During a cross-data-center partition, the business prefers brief stale reads over losing local low-latency availability.
q: 这体现了哪条取舍？
q_en: Which tradeoff does this show?
options: CAP/PACELC 中可用性和低延迟优先于强一致
LRU 和 LFU 的内存占用完全相同
换网络协议会自动解决跨地域一致性
hash table 必须持久化到磁盘
options_en: In CAP/PACELC terms, availability and low latency are preferred over strong consistency
LRU and LFU have exactly the same memory footprint
Changing the network protocol automatically solves cross-region consistency
A hash table must be persisted to disk
why: 跨地域缓存常把可用性和延迟放在强一致前面，因为缓存本来是加速层。关键是把可接受的 staleness 窗口说清楚并监控复制延迟。
why_en: Cross-region caches often prefer availability and latency over strict freshness, as long as staleness is bounded and monitored.
tradeoff: 可用性与低延迟 vs 强一致

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 描述分布式系统在网络分区下强一致和可用性的取舍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP describes the tradeoff between consistency and availability during a network partition.

termDefinitions.fullName: Partition Availability Consistency Else Latency Consistency
termDefinitions.meaning: PACELC 补充说明没有分区时也常在延迟和一致性之间取舍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PACELC adds that even without a partition, systems often trade latency against consistency.

optionExplanations: 对，分区期间宁可短暂读旧值也要保持本地可用和低延迟，这正是 PACELC 里牺牲一致性换延迟的取舍。
LRU 和 LFU 要额外维护的元数据不一样，内存占用通常不同，这跟这里问的一致性取舍也不是一回事。
换传输协议解决的是网络层问题，副本之间数据什么时候收敛是复制语义决定的，协议换不了这个。
hash table 是内存索引结构，要不要持久化是另一个设计决策，跟这里描述的可用性取舍无关。
optionExplanations_en: Right—accepting brief stale reads to keep local service available and fast during a partition is exactly PACELC's latency-over-consistency choice.
LRU and LFU track different metadata, so their memory footprint usually isn't the same—also a different topic from this consistency tradeoff.
Swapping the network protocol is a transport-layer change; replica convergence timing is decided by replication semantics, not the protocol.
A hash table is an in-memory index; whether to persist it is a separate design decision, unrelated to the availability tradeoff described here.

scenario: 一个读多写少的服务只需要缓存序列化后的对象字符串；团队希望系统简单、水平扩展容易、主要吃多核网络吞吐。
scenario_en: A read-heavy service only caches serialized object strings and wants a simple horizontally scalable system that uses multicore throughput.
q: Memcached 和 Redis 中更直接的选择是什么？
q_en: Between Memcached and Redis, which is the more direct choice?
options: Redis，因为必须使用 Lua 和 geospatial
Memcached，因为简单 string KV 和多线程更贴合
Apache Ignite，因为一定要分布式 SQL
Hazelcast，因为一定要商业授权
options_en: Redis, because Lua and geospatial features are mandatory
Memcached, because simple string KV and multithreading fit the workload
Apache Ignite, because distributed SQL is mandatory
Hazelcast, because commercial licensing is mandatory
why: Memcached 擅长简单 key-string 缓存，shared-nothing 加客户端路由让水平扩展很直观。代价是持久化、复制和复杂数据结构要靠外部方案。
why_en: Memcached fits simple read-heavy string caching with straightforward horizontal scaling.
whenOtherWins: 如果要原生 list、sorted set、持久化或内置故障转移，Redis 更合适。
tradeoff: 简单吞吐与多线程 vs 内建高级能力

termDefinitions.meaning: shared-nothing 表示各缓存服务器独立工作，不共享本地状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Shared-nothing means servers operate independently without sharing local state.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lua 是 Redis 可执行脚本常用的轻量脚本语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lua is a lightweight scripting language commonly used for Redis scripts.

optionExplanations: 题目里没有要求 Lua 脚本或地理位置查询，这里硬加的前提本身就不成立。
对，只缓存序列化字符串、要简单和多核吞吐，正贴合 Memcached 的 shared-nothing 多线程模型。
题目没有要分布式 SQL 这个需求，Apache Ignite 的强项跟这里描述的简单场景不匹配。
商业授权不是这里给的约束，用许可条款做决策依据跟题目描述的技术需求没关系。
optionExplanations_en: Nothing in the scenario requires Lua scripting or geospatial queries—that premise doesn't hold here.
Right—caching only serialized strings with simple, multicore throughput fits Memcached's shared-nothing multithreaded model.
The scenario never asks for distributed SQL, so Apache Ignite's strengths don't match what's described here.
Commercial licensing isn't a constraint given in the scenario—basing the choice on licensing ignores the actual technical need.

scenario: 缓存对象是排行榜、集合和 hash map，服务还希望缓存层自带复制、故障转移和可选持久化。
scenario_en: The cache needs leaderboards, sets, and hash maps, plus built-in replication, failover, and optional persistence.
q: Memcached 和 Redis 中更直接的选择是什么？
q_en: Between Memcached and Redis, which is the more direct choice?
options: Memcached，因为它原生支持 sorted set
Redis，因为它支持多种数据结构和内建 HA 能力
纯 HTTP CDN，因为它能执行所有集合操作
只用本地进程变量，因为它天然跨机复制
options_en: Memcached, because it natively supports sorted sets
Redis, because it supports multiple data structures and built-in HA features
A pure HTTP CDN, because it can execute all set operations
Only local process variables, because they naturally replicate across machines
why: Redis 不只是 string KV，它能在服务端操作 list、set、sorted set、hash 等结构，并提供 Sentinel、Cluster、持久化选项。代价是系统能力更丰富，运维和一致性边界也更复杂。
why_en: Redis fits richer cache behavior because it has native data structures plus built-in replication, failover, and persistence options.
whenOtherWins: 如果只缓存字符串且追求极简多线程吞吐，Memcached 更省心。
tradeoff: 丰富功能与内建 HA vs 简单性

termDefinitions.meaning: HA 表示系统在部分组件故障时仍能继续服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: High Availability means the system keeps serving despite some component failures.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Sentinel 监控 Redis 主从并在主节点故障时触发故障转移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Sentinel monitors Redis primary-replica setups and triggers failover.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Cluster 提供 Redis 的自动分片和主从副本管理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Cluster provides automatic sharding and primary-replica management for Redis.

optionExplanations: Memcached 只是简单 string KV，没有原生 sorted set，这个前提本身就不成立。
对，Redis 服务端原生就能操作集合、有序集合和哈希这些结构，还自带主从故障转移和可选落盘，排行榜加高可用一次覆盖。
CDN 是边缘静态内容分发，不是通用数据结构存储，做不了集合运算。
本地进程变量只存在于单个进程内，不会自动跨机复制，这个说法本身就错。
optionExplanations_en: Memcached is a plain string KV store with no native sorted sets—that premise is false.
Right—Redis natively supports list/set/sorted-set/hash plus Sentinel, Cluster, and optional persistence, covering leaderboards and built-in HA together.
A CDN distributes static content at the edge; it isn't a general data-structure store and can't run set operations.
Local process variables live inside one process only—they don't replicate across machines on their own.

scenario: 面试官让你用一句话比较 Redis 和 Memcached，不要把两者说成谁全局更好。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks for a concise Redis-versus-Memcached comparison without claiming one is globally better.
q: 哪条比较最像面试答案？
q_en: Which comparison sounds most interview-ready?
options: Memcached 偏简单 string cache；Redis 偏多结构、持久化和复制
Memcached 是关系数据库；Redis 只能存页面片段和静态 HTML
Redis 永远强一致；Memcached 永远不能水平扩容或做客户端路由
两者都只支持离线归档，不能作为在线缓存，也没有性能差异
options_en: Memcached is a simple string cache; Redis adds data structures, persistence, and replication
Memcached is a relational database; Redis can only store page fragments and static HTML
Redis is always strongly consistent; Memcached can never scale out or use client routing
Both are only offline archives, cannot serve online caching, and have no performance difference
why: 这个回答按能力边界比较，而不是贴好坏标签。真实选择要看数据结构、持久化、复制和运维复杂度。
why_en: The useful comparison is about capability boundaries, not a global winner.
tradeoff: 极简缓存吞吐 vs 丰富服务端能力

termDefinitions.meaning: AOF 是 Redis 记录写命令以便恢复数据的持久化日志。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Append Only File is a Redis persistence log that records write commands for recovery.

termDefinitions.meaning: RDB 是 Redis 的快照式持久化文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Database is Redis's snapshot-style persistence file.

optionExplanations: 对，这条按能力边界说话：Memcached 专精简单字符串缓存，Redis 多加了数据结构、持久化和复制，没有贴标签说谁全局更好。
Memcached 是内存缓存，不是关系数据库；Redis 存的也远不止页面片段或静态 HTML。
Redis 不是永远强一致，Memcached 用客户端一致性哈希也能水平扩容，这两个绝对化说法都不成立。
两者都是常用的在线缓存系统，不是离线归档工具，也确实存在真实的性能差异。
optionExplanations_en: Right—this stays at the capability level: Memcached is a simple string cache, Redis adds structures, persistence, and replication, without crowning a global winner.
Memcached is an in-memory cache, not a relational database; Redis stores far more than page fragments or static HTML.
Redis isn't always strongly consistent, and Memcached can scale out via client-side hashing—both absolute claims are false.
Both are common online caching systems, not offline archives, and there is a real performance difference between them.

scenario: 客户端要连续发 100 个 Redis GET。每次等响应再发下一个时，RTT 和 socket 调用占了大量时间。
scenario_en: A client needs to send 100 Redis GETs; waiting for each response before sending the next wastes RTTs and socket calls.
q: Redis pipelining 优化的是什么？
q_en: What does Redis pipelining optimize?
options: 把多个请求先发出去，减少等待往返和系统调用开销
让 Redis 服务器并行执行同一个 key 的所有写
自动把所有命令持久化为 SQL
删除客户端批处理逻辑
options_en: Send multiple requests before waiting, reducing round trips and syscall overhead
Make the Redis server execute all writes to one key in parallel
Automatically persist every command as SQL
Remove batching logic from the client
why: pipelining 省的是客户端等待 RTT、socket I/O 和系统调用，不是把单个 Redis 实例变成并行执行引擎。批量越多、距离越远，收益越明显。
why_en: Pipelining improves throughput by batching network round trips, not by making one Redis server execute commands in parallel.
tradeoff: 吞吐与 RTT amortization vs 客户端批量管理
codeSample:
redis-cli --pipe <<'EOF'
GET user:1
GET user:2
GET user:3
EOF
# 客户端连续发送命令，再批量读取响应。

termDefinitions.meaning: socket I/O 是进程通过网络套接字读写数据的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Socket I/O is reading or writing data through a network socket.

optionExplanations: 对，pipelining 让客户端把多条命令连续发出去、不必每条都等回包，省下的是网络往返次数和逐次系统调用的开销。
Redis 命令在单线程里顺序执行，这个机制省下来的是网络等待和逐次系统调用，不会让服务端对同一个 key 并行处理写。
pipelining 只是批量发命令，不涉及把命令转成 SQL 或做持久化。
pipelining 恰恰是客户端主动做批量发送，说它删除批处理逻辑正好说反了。
optionExplanations_en: Right—pipelining lets the client fire multiple commands before waiting, saving round-trip waits and per-command syscall overhead.
Redis executes commands on one thread; pipelining saves network round trips, it doesn't make the server parallelize writes to one key.
Pipelining just batches command sending—it has nothing to do with converting commands to SQL or persisting them.
Pipelining is the client deliberately batching sends—saying it removes batching logic gets it backwards.

scenario: Memcached 用 slab allocation 管理内存。团队发现某些对象变大后，内存碎片少了，但小对象所在 slab 有浪费。
scenario_en: Memcached uses slab allocation; fragmentation is lower, but some slabs waste space for smaller objects.
q: slab allocation 的典型取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the typical tradeoff of slab allocation?
options: 减少碎片，但对象尺寸不匹配时会浪费空间
保证每个对象都强一致复制
让所有对象自动变成 Redis sorted set
禁止缓存大于 1KB 的对象
options_en: It reduces fragmentation but can waste space when object sizes do not fit well
It guarantees strongly consistent replication for every object
It turns every object into a Redis sorted set
It forbids caching objects larger than 1 KB
why: slab 把内存按尺寸类别分配，能控制碎片；但对象大小落在不合适的类别里，会留下未用空间。它解决的是内存管理，不是复制一致性。
why_en: Slab allocation manages fragmentation by size classes, but mismatched object sizes can waste memory.
tradeoff: 碎片控制 vs 尺寸类别浪费

termDefinitions.meaning: slab allocation 按固定大小类别分配内存块，减少外部碎片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Slab allocation assigns memory from fixed-size classes to reduce external fragmentation.

optionExplanations: 对，slab 按固定尺寸类别分配内存能控制外部碎片，但对象大小落不进合适类别时那部分空间就浪费了。
它管的是单机内存怎么切块分配，不涉及跨节点复制要不要强一致。
这套机制是 Memcached 自己的内存布局方案，不会让对象变成 Redis 的数据结构。
slab allocation 不禁止大对象，只是不同尺寸类别对应不同 slab，跟固定容量上限没关系。
optionExplanations_en: Right—slab allocation controls external fragmentation with fixed size classes, but space is wasted when an object doesn't fit its class well.
Slab allocation is about how one machine's memory is carved up—it says nothing about cross-node replication consistency.
Slab allocation is Memcached's own memory layout scheme; it doesn't turn objects into Redis data structures.
Slab allocation doesn't forbid large objects—it just maps different sizes to different classes, no hard size cap involved.

scenario: 缓存值经常超过 100KB，读写主要消耗 CPU 和网络吞吐；团队不需要 Redis 的复杂数据结构。
scenario_en: Cached values are often larger than 100 KB, the workload is CPU/network heavy, and Redis data structures are not needed.
q: 在 Memcached 与单进程 Redis 之间倾向谁？
q_en: Between Memcached and a single Redis process, which way would you lean?
options: Memcached，因为多线程更能利用多核处理大对象吞吐
Redis，因为单进程一定更适合大对象
两者都必须禁用网络
只用 Bloom filter 存完整 value
options_en: Memcached, because multithreading can use multiple cores for large-object throughput
Redis, because a single process is always better for large objects
Both must disable networking
Use only a Bloom filter to store full values
why: 大对象缓存更容易吃 CPU、copy 和网络，Memcached 多线程能更自然地利用多核。代价是你放弃 Redis 的数据结构、脚本和内建复制能力。
why_en: For large simple values, Memcached's multithreading can use multiple cores more directly.
whenOtherWins: 如果大对象还需要 Redis 原生命令、持久化或 Cluster 管理，Redis 仍可能更合适。
tradeoff: 多核吞吐 vs Redis 高级能力

termDefinitions.meaning: Bloom filter 是概率型成员测试结构，能判断一定不存在，但可能误报存在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic membership structure that can say definitely absent but may have false positives.

optionExplanations: 对，大对象处理更吃 CPU 和 copy 开销，Memcached 的多线程模型能让多核一起分担这部分工作。
单进程处理大对象反而更容易被单核吞吐卡住，说单进程一定更适合站不住脚。
缓存服务器要通过网络被访问，禁用网络等于让缓存没法被读写，这不是可行方案。
Bloom filter 只能做成员测试返回可能存在或一定不存在，存不了完整 value，答不了这里的需求。
optionExplanations_en: Right—large objects cost more CPU and copying, and Memcached's multithreaded model lets multiple cores share that work.
A single process handling large objects is more likely to bottleneck on one core—'always better' doesn't hold up.
A cache server has to be reachable over the network; disabling it entirely means nothing can read or write the cache.
A Bloom filter only answers maybe-present or definitely-absent—it can't store the full value, so it can't meet this need.

scenario: 缓存前面有一批随机 key 查询，其中大量 key 根本不存在。你想尽早挡掉不存在的 key，减少缓存和数据库无效查询。
scenario_en: Many random key lookups are for keys that do not exist; you want to reject impossible keys before hitting cache or database.
q: Bloom filter 能提供什么帮助？
q_en: How can a Bloom filter help?
options: 快速判断某个 key 一定不存在
精确返回 key 的完整 value
保证所有存在判断都没有误报
替代缓存驱逐策略
options_en: Quickly tell that a key is definitely absent
Return the full value for a key exactly
Guarantee no false positives in membership tests
Replace cache eviction policy
why: Bloom filter 适合做成员测试：不存在可以直接挡掉，可能存在才继续查。代价是假阳性，可能让少量不存在的 key 继续走后端。
why_en: A Bloom filter can reject definitely absent keys early, while false positives may still pass through.
whenOtherWins: 如果必须精确枚举或取回 value，应该查索引、缓存或数据库。
tradeoff: 低内存成员测试 vs 假阳性
optionExplanations: 对，Bloom filter 命中「不存在」时结果是确定的，能在查缓存和数据库之前就先挡掉这些请求。
它本身不存 value，只回答成员测试，真正取值还是要靠缓存或数据库来做。
假阳性是 Bloom filter 与生俱来的代价，说它保证零误报的说法本身就站不住。
Bloom filter 解决的是要不要继续查下去，不管内存满了该淘汰哪个已缓存条目。
optionExplanations_en: Right—when a Bloom filter says 'absent,' that's certain, so it can reject those lookups before they ever hit cache or database.
A Bloom filter doesn't store values at all—it only answers membership tests; you still need cache or database for the actual data.
False positives are an inherent property of Bloom filters, so claiming zero false positives gets it backwards.
A Bloom filter decides whether to keep looking, not which already-cached entry to discard when memory is full.

scenario: 上线缓存后，用户仍报告延迟波动。你需要判断是命中率下降、节点过载、还是回源数据库变慢。
scenario_en: After launching the cache, users still report latency spikes; you need to tell whether hit rate fell, nodes overloaded, or database fallback slowed.
q: 监控首先要看哪些指标？
q_en: Which metrics should you inspect first?
options: hit/miss rate、节点 CPU/内存、回源延迟
只看代码行数和文件数量，忽略运行时请求路径
只看产品页面颜色和按钮文案，忽略后端延迟
只看缓存 key 是否按字母排序，忽略命中率
options_en: Hit/miss rate, node CPU/memory, and fallback latency
Only lines of code and file count, ignoring runtime request paths
Only product page colors and button copy, ignoring backend latency
Only whether cache keys are alphabetically sorted, ignoring hit rate
why: hit/miss rate 说明缓存有没有挡住读，节点资源说明缓存层是否过载，回源延迟说明 miss 的代价。三者合起来才能定位延迟波动。
why_en: Hit rate, cache-node resources, and fallback latency together explain where cache latency is coming from.
whenOtherWins: 如果是功能正确性事故，还要优先看错误率、旧值比例和失效日志。
tradeoff: 可观测性成本 vs 快速定位

termDefinitions.meaning: hit rate 是请求直接从缓存返回的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hit rate is the fraction of requests served directly from cache.

optionExplanations: 对，这三类指标分别对应缓存命中、节点健康和回源代价，缺一个都定位不到真正的瓶颈。
代码行数和文件数量跟运行时请求路径没有关系，看不出延迟波动来自哪里。
页面颜色和按钮文案是前端展示问题，跟后端延迟的根因完全是两回事。
key 是否按字母排序不影响命中率或延迟，这个指标对定位问题没有帮助。
optionExplanations_en: Right—hit rate shows whether the cache is absorbing reads, node resources show overload, and fallback latency shows the miss cost; together they locate the spike.
Lines of code and file count say nothing about the runtime request path, so they can't explain where latency comes from.
Page colors and button copy are frontend concerns, completely separate from the backend latency root cause.
Whether keys are alphabetically sorted doesn't affect hit rate or latency—this metric won't help locate the problem.

q: 一个 cache-aside 分布式缓存读请求的完整状态链是什么？
q_en: What is the full state chain for a cache-aside read in a distributed cache?
steps: 缓存 miss 时，服务回源数据库读取权威值。
缓存客户端用 consistent hashing 选择目标缓存节点。
服务把值写回缓存，并设置合适 TTL。
客户端请求到达服务，服务内的缓存客户端接管读路径。
命中则直接从缓存返回；未命中才进入回源链路。
why: 这条链把客户端路由、命中返回、miss 回源和回填都串起来。代价是 miss 会放大到数据库，所以要监控命中率和回源延迟。
why_en: The read path routes to a cache node first, then falls back to the database only on a miss.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Req[Request] --> Client[Cache client]
  Client --> Hash[Consistent hash]
  Hash --> Node[Cache node]
  Node -- hit --> Resp[Return]
  Node -- miss --> DB[(DB)]
  DB --> Fill[Set cache TTL]
  Fill --> Resp

scenario: 面试官让你设计分布式缓存，并特别强调 invalidation、replication、高并发、低延迟和高吞吐。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to design a distributed cache, emphasizing invalidation, replication, high concurrency, low latency, and high throughput.
q: 开场设计回答应按什么顺序组织？
q_en: How should you structure the opening design answer?
steps: 再讲分片路由、缓存客户端和 consistent hashing。
最后补复制、失效、热 key、监控和失败恢复。
先澄清读写比例、数据新鲜度、容量、延迟和故障目标。
说明 API：put/get/delete 或 invalidate 的语义。
选择读写策略：cache-aside/read-through 与 write-through/write-back/write-around。
why: 我会先把约束问清楚，再落 API 和策略，最后展开分片、复制和故障。这样回答不会一上来堆技术名词，而是每个组件都被需求牵引。
why_en: Start with constraints, then APIs and policies, and only then expand into sharding, replication, and failure handling.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官已经给了完整约束，可以直接从 API 和高层架构开始。
tradeoff: 需求牵引设计 vs 技术清单堆叠

q: 设计分布式缓存时，哪些非功能需求通常要主动说清楚？
q_en: Which non-functional requirements should you clarify when designing a distributed cache?
options: 低延迟读写
水平扩展
高可用和故障降级
缓存必须永久保存所有数据
options_en: Low-latency reads and writes
Horizontal scalability
High availability and failure degradation
The cache must permanently store all data
why: 缓存设计通常围绕性能、扩展、可用性、一致性和成本展开。永久保存所有数据是数据库或持久 KV 的职责，不是普通缓存的默认目标。
why_en: Distributed-cache requirements usually center on latency, scalability, availability, consistency, and cost.
optionExplanations: 低延迟读写是缓存要交付的核心价值，必须明确说清楚目标是几毫秒还是几十毫秒。
水平扩展决定了容量和吞吐能不能靠加机器一起增长，是设计分片和路由的前提。
高可用和故障降级说明单点或单 DC 出问题时系统该怎么继续服务，不说清楚会漏掉容错设计。
错，永久保存所有数据是持久数据库或 KV 存储的职责，普通缓存默认允许驱逐和重建。
optionExplanations_en: Low-latency reads and writes are the core value a cache delivers—you need to pin down whether that means single-digit or tens of milliseconds.
Horizontal scalability determines whether capacity and throughput can grow by adding machines, driving sharding and routing decisions.
High availability and degradation define how the system keeps serving when a node or data center fails—skip it and fault tolerance gets missed.
Wrong—permanently storing all data is a durable database or KV store's job; an ordinary cache is expected to evict and rebuild.

scenario: 团队要缓存海量热门数据，但预算有限；如果用专用高端硬件，缓存层成本会超过数据库优化本身。
scenario_en: The team needs to cache many hot objects on a limited budget; specialized hardware would make the cache more expensive than the database optimization.
q: 硬件选择应遵循什么原则？
q_en: What hardware principle should guide the cache tier?
options: 优先用 commodity hardware 横向扩展
只买最贵的专用硬件，即使成本超过数据库优化
把在线缓存放到离线磁带库，再靠人工读取
禁止增加任何缓存节点，让单机承担全部增长
options_en: Prefer commodity hardware and scale horizontally
Buy only the most expensive specialized hardware, even if it costs more than DB tuning
Put the online cache on offline tape and rely on manual reads
Forbid adding cache nodes and make one machine absorb all growth
why: 缓存层的价值是用相对便宜的内存机器挡住昂贵后端读，而不是造一个更贵的后端。commodity hardware 加分片和复制能把成本、容量和可用性一起摊开。
why_en: Commodity cache nodes preserve the cost advantage while sharding and replication provide scale and availability.
whenOtherWins: 如果是极端低延迟交易系统，专用硬件可能值得单独评估。
tradeoff: 单位成本与水平扩展 vs 专用硬件性能

termDefinitions.meaning: commodity hardware 是常规可采购服务器，单机不特殊，靠数量和架构扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Commodity hardware means standard servers whose scale comes from quantity and architecture rather than specialized machines.

optionExplanations: 对，用大量常规服务器堆分片和副本，比造更贵的专用后端更划算，成本随规模平滑增长。
只买最贵的专用硬件会让缓存层比它要保护的数据库优化本身还贵，跟预算有限的前提直接冲突。
离线磁带要人工介入读取，延迟是分钟到小时级，完全不能承担在线热读的角色。
禁止增加节点会让单机独自扛住全部增长，容量和可用性都撑不住，也不省钱。
optionExplanations_en: Right—commodity hardware plus sharding and replication builds capacity and availability from quantity, scaling cost linearly instead of jumping.
Buying only the most expensive specialized hardware would make the cache tier pricier than the database optimization it protects—against the budget.
Offline tape needs manual intervention to read, with minutes-to-hours latency—it can't play an online hot-read role at all.
Forbidding new nodes forces one machine to absorb all growth, failing both capacity and availability, and it doesn't even save money.
